# Textbooks and general resources {#sec-textbooks}

## Textbooks

No single textbook is required. These cover most of the material, but none
is fully up to date.

- @zvelebil2008 — *Understanding Bioinformatics*. Broad coverage, recommended in the exam description.
- @pevsner2015 — *Bioinformatics and Functional Genomics*. Broad coverage; the basis of the 2021 exam variant.
- @jones2004 — *An Introduction to Bioinformatics Algorithms*. Algorithms: alignment, suffix trees, assembly, phylogeny, motifs.
- @compeau2018 — *Bioinformatics Algorithms: An Active Learning Approach*. With free online lectures.
- @durbin1998 — *Biological Sequence Analysis*. The classic on probabilistic models and HMMs.
- @felsenstein2004 — *Inferring Phylogenies*.
- @burkowski2008 — *Structural Bioinformatics: An Algorithmic Approach*. Structure, dynamic programming, RNA secondary structure, superposition, machine learning.
- @gagniuc2021 — *Algorithms in Bioinformatics: Theory and Implementation*. Alignment, motifs, Markov chains.
- @hastie2009 — *The Elements of Statistical Learning*.

## Keeping up to date

- Proceedings of the most recent **ISMB** and **ECCB** conferences (published as supplements of *Bioinformatics*).
- The annual *Nucleic Acids Research* **Database** and **Web Server** issues.
- Seminars and dissertations at DBB and SciLifeLab.

## Collections of papers

- [Classical papers in bioinformatics (Elofsson group)](https://sites.google.com/a/scilifelab.se/elofsson/teaching/classical-papers)
